content: Structural and non-structural damage to facilities may occur, either partially or completely. Buildings may collapse due to coastal erosion and material corrosion. There may be an increased need for water treatment, such as through desalination processes. Maintenance and repair requirements for facility buildings may rise significantly. Facilities may experience recurrent flooding during high tide events. Transportation systems may become obstructed, and ambulance stations may be flooded, hindering emergency response. Access to buildings may be blocked, preventing entry or evacuation. Critical medical equipment may sustain damage, impairing its functionality. Essential supplies, including medications, treatments, medical devices, drugs, laboratory supplies, pharmaceuticals, vaccines, blood, milk, nutritional supplies, and other critical items, may be damaged and require immediate repositioning. Complex and emergency healthcare services, such as surgeries, advanced treatments, urgent care, and blood bank operations, may be disrupted.
